channel.title: SoutheastAEC™ — Building Science & Envelope Specifications
channel.description: Independent building science publication analyzing inward vapor drive, unvented crawlspace dehumidification, hurricane wind shear tie-downs, and coastal moisture control across the American Southeast.

item.title: How to Air-Seal Attic Ductwork and Ceiling Chases: Blower Door Diagnostics and Mastic Sealing
item.description: Condition: Leaky attic ducts pull 140°F humid air into Southern homes. Need: Air-seal ceiling planes and ductwork. Action: Diagnose leaks with blower doors, seal boots with fiberglass mesh and mastic, and foam top plates. Result: Slashing cooling loads and hitting < 3.0 ACH50.

item.title: How to Apply Borate Wood Treatments to Structural Framing: Jobsite Protocol
item.description: Condition: Exposed framing lumber remains vulnerable to termites and decay fungi. Need: Field-applied borate preservation. Action: Mix DOT solution with hot water, spray 2 coats at 25 PSI, and verify penetration. Result: Lifetime wood immunity to termites and fungal decay.

item.title: Closed-Cell Spray Foam in Coastal Flood Zones: FEMA Class 5 Washout Resilience
item.description: Condition: Coastal storm surge floods living spaces and ruins fibrous insulation. Need: Submersible flood-damage resistant insulation. Action: Specify 2.0-lb closed-cell spray foam qualifying as a FEMA Class 5 material under ASCE 24. Result: Zero water absorption and rapid post-flood recovery.

item.title: Concrete Block Stucco Waterproofing: Elastomeric Coatings and Window Flashing
item.description: Condition: Tropical rainstorms penetrate porous Florida CBS stucco walls. Need: Continuous exterior waterproofing and flashing. Action: Apply high-build elastomeric acrylic coatings, form sloped sill pans, and flash window bucks. Result: Moisture-impermeable, crack-bridging masonry envelopes.

item.title: Concrete Slab Moisture Barriers and LVP Adhesive Failure in Coastal Groundwaters
item.description: Condition: Shallow coastal water tables push moisture through unsealed slabs, ruining luxury vinyl plank. Need: Hydrostatic vapor mitigation. Action: Test in-situ RH with ASTM F2170 and install ASTM F3010 epoxy moisture barriers. Result: Stop adhesive breakdown and prevent floor cupping.

item.title: Cool Roof Solar Reflectance Index (SRI) in Climate Zones 2A & 3A: Reducing Attic Heat Loads
item.description: Condition: Dark roofs absorb intense solar radiation, heating attics to 145°F. Need: High-albedo radiant rejection. Action: Specify cool roof materials with Solar Reflectance Index (SRI > 82) under ASTM E1980. Result: Lower attic temperatures by 30°F and slash cooling loads by 35%.

item.title: Crawlspace Encapsulation in Hot-Humid Climates: Vapor Retarders, Vent Sealing, and Low-Grain Dehumidification
item.description: Hot-humid coastal climates overwhelm open foundation vents with 75°F dew points, rotting subfloors. Learn how IRC R408.3 sealed encapsulation with 20-mil vapor retarders and low-grain dehumidifiers eliminates wood decay fungi.

item.title: How to Encapsulate a Crawlspace in the Southeast: Step-by-Step Installation Guide
item.description: Condition: Southern dirt crawlspaces sweat in summer humidity. Need: Code-compliant encapsulation under IRC R408.3. Action: Grade soil, install 20-mil Class A liner, seal masonry vents, and hardwire an LGR dehumidifier. Result: Permanent moisture stabilization under 55% RH.

item.title: Formosan Subterranean Termite Defense: Pressure-Treated Borate Lumber and Physical Barriers
item.description: Condition: Formosan subterranean termites devastate Southern structural timber. Need: Building-science termite immunity. Action: Specify DOT borate-treated framing, 316 stainless mesh barriers, and crushed granite sands. Result: Permanent wood protection and carton nest prevention.

item.title: Heat Pump Water Heaters in Hot-Humid Climates: The Subtropical Efficiency Hack
item.description: Condition: Southern water heating wastes 18% of residential electricity. Need: Energy-efficient hot water generation. Action: Install hybrid heat pump water heaters in unconditioned garages. Result: Cut water heating power by 70% while gaining free 55°F air conditioning and dehumidification.

item.title: Hurricane-Rated Garage Door Reinforcement: U-Bar Struts and Track Hardening
item.description: Condition: Garage doors represent the most vulnerable opening to hurricane blowouts. Need: Structural wind load hardening. Action: Install 20-gauge steel U-bar struts, 11-gauge track brackets, and vertical locking posts. Result: Eliminate door collapse and prevent roof uplift.

item.title: Hurricane Shutters vs. Impact-Resistant Glass: Installed Cost, Deployment, and Insurance ROI
item.description: Condition: Coastal homeowners face high hurricane wind risks and soaring insurance costs. Need: Cost-benefit analysis of opening protection. Action: Compare 5 shutter and impact glass systems across cost, deployment, and ROI. Result: Maximize wind credits and storm security.

item.title: How to Retrofit Hurricane Straps and Rafter Tie-Downs: Continuous Load Path Engineering
item.description: Condition: Pre-2002 Southern homes lack continuous hurricane load paths. Need: FBC-compliant retrofit tie-downs. Action: Install Simpson H10A straps, anchor masonry clips, and drive structural screws into top plates. Result: Uplift resistance exceeding 1,200 lbs per truss.

item.title: How to Level a Pier-and-Beam Foundation: Hydraulic Bottle Jacks, Cribbing, and Steel Shims
item.description: Condition: Sagging historic pier-and-beam floors bind doors and crack plaster. Need: Safe structural leveling protocol. Action: Build timber cribbing, operate 20-ton hydraulic jacks in 1/8-inch daily lifts, and set steel shims. Result: Restored level floors without structural damage.

item.title: Impact-Resistant Windows in High-Velocity Hurricane Zones: NOA, SentryGlas vs. PVB, and ASTM E1996
item.description: Condition: Category 5 hurricanes launch deadly flying debris at building envelopes. Need: HVHZ-compliant impact glazing. Action: Specify SentryGlas ionoplast interlayers, reinforced framing, and Miami-Dade NOA ratings. Result: Unbroken building envelopes under 9,000 pressure cycles.

item.title: Inward Vapor Drive and the Vinyl Wallpaper Mold Disaster: Thermodynamic Envelope Failures in the South
item.description: Condition: Hot-humid summer air drives moisture inward through exterior cladding. Need: Prevent interstitial wall cavity mold. Action: Eliminate low-perm vinyl wallpaper, install rainscreen drainage cavities, and use permeable latex finishes. Result: Dry, mold-free gypsum assemblies.

item.title: How to Apply Liquid-Applied Flashing to CBS Rough Openings: Step-by-Step Guide
item.description: Condition: Wind-driven rain penetrates unsealed window bucks in Florida CBS homes. Need: Seamless rough opening waterproofing. Action: Slope masonry sills, tool liquid-applied elastomeric flashing at 60 mils, and bed frames under ASTM E2112. Result: Watertight, monolithic sill protection.

item.title: Historic Pier-and-Beam Foundation Restoration: Soil Subsidence, Rotted Sills, and Pier Sizing
item.description: Condition: Historic Southern pier-and-beam cottages sag from soft clays and rotted sills. Need: Structural restoration without cracking plaster. Action: Shore framing with timber cribbing, replace sills with UC4B lumber, and resize footings. Result: Level floors and historic preservation.

item.title: Soffit Vent Blowout and Hurricane Wind-Driven Rain: Preventing Ceiling Collapse
item.description: Condition: Hurricane winds dislodge lightweight soffit panels, funneling rain into attics. Need: Code-compliant soffit wind reinforcement. Action: Install reinforced fascia sub-framing, fastened panels, and baffled vents under FBC 1709.10. Result: Watertight eaves and ceiling protection.

item.title: Spray Foam Unvented Attics Under Florida Building Code: R806.5 Insulation and HVAC Protection
item.description: Condition: Vented Florida attics reach 140°F, sweating HVAC ducts and wasting energy. Need: FBC R806.5 unvented attic compliance. Action: Spray closed-cell or open-cell polyurethane to roof decks and seal soffits. Result: Lower cooling loads and zero duct condensation.

item.title: Standing Seam vs. 5V Crimp Metal Roofing: Coastal Wind and Salt-Spray Performance
item.description: Condition: Coastal hurricane zones face 140+ MPH winds and marine salt fog. Need: Wind-resilient metal roofing. Action: Compare 24-gauge concealed-clip standing seam vs. exposed 5V crimp panels under TAS 125. Result: Eliminate fastener gasket dry-rot and prevent sheet tear-off.

item.title: Variable-Speed Inverter Heat Pumps for Humidity Control: Low-Stage Run Times and Latent Physics
item.description: Condition: Single-stage AC short-cycling leaves high humidity in Southern homes. Need: Extended latent moisture extraction. Action: Deploy variable-speed inverter heat pumps operating at 30% capacity. Result: Continuous dehumidification and up to 40% energy savings.

item.title: Whole-Home Dehumidifiers vs. Oversized AC: Taming Latent Heat in the Humid South
item.description: Condition: Southern homes suffer cold, clammy 70°F indoor air at 70% RH. Need: Decouple sensible and latent cooling. Action: Replace oversized AC short-cycling with dedicated central dehumidifiers (Santa Fe/Ultra-Aire). Result: Stable 48% RH and mold-free envelopes.
